newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MANDELA MEETS SOUTH AFRICA AND INDIA TEAMS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MANDELA MEETS SOUTH AFRICA AND INDIA TEAMS.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela congratulated South Africans on avoiding "another Bosnia" when he made a morale-boosting visit to the second cricket test in Cape Town on Saturday.
The South African president arrived 20 minutes before the lunch interval and was introduced to both teams on the pitch.
Interviewed live on SABC television and for Indian Star TV Mandela was asked to give a new year message to South Africans.
He said: "Although I was born and brought up here I thought I didn't know this country because almost everybody was predicting that we were going to have another Bosnia.

"But all the sections of the community, black, coloured, Indian and white have co-operated very well to make it possible to have this smooth and peaceful transformation and we congratulate everybody."

The sports-mad politician for once chose not to wear a national team blazer but sported a sun hat bearing the King Protea -- the emblem of the national cricket team -- as he was given a standing ovation by a Newlands full house of 17,000.
Mandela famously appeared at the rugby union World Cup and African Nations soccer cup in national team jerseys.
On both occasions it coincided with historic victories for the Springboks and Bafana Bafana.
He said he now hoped South Africa would be able to host the 2004 Olympics in Cape Town.

"We have done everything to ensure that the decision of the IOC will be favourable to us," he said. "We are hopeful. We have demonstrated especially during the rugby World Cup that we can hold an international sporting event in a very successful and efficient manner."

His arrival at Newlands coincided with another good day for South African sportsmen. Having notched up a post-isolation highest score of 529 for seven declared, South Africa had India in deep trouble at 145 for five at the lunch interval.
